en.name: Grilled eel
en.summary: Kabayaki is eel split, steamed, grilled and lacquered with a sweet soy glaze, sold chilled or frozen in vacuum packs. Follow the printed date while the pack is sealed; once it is open, 3–4 days in the fridge and 1–2 months in the freezer.
en.pantry: Kabayaki is a chilled or frozen cooked food, not a shelf-stable one. The sweet glaze looks like a preserve and is not: it is sugar and soy on the surface of a moist, fully cooked, oily fish. A vacuum pack bought from a chiller stays in the chiller. Follow the 2-hour rule once it is out, or 1 hour if the kitchen is above 32 °C (90 °F), and reheat it properly rather than letting it sit warm on the counter while the rice finishes.
en.fridge: An unopened pack goes by its own printed date, which reflects how the pack was made and is longer than anything we could give. Once the vacuum pack is opened it is simply cooked fish: keep it at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a covered box and eat it within 3–4 days, the published figure for cooked fish. Store it away from strong-smelling food; the glaze picks up odours. Reheat it through rather than warming it, and do not re-cool and re-serve the same portion repeatedly.
en.freezer: Kabayaki keeps 1–2 months at −18 °C (0 °F). Freeze it in the unopened pack if you can, or wrap portions tightly with the glaze intact. The best way to reheat is straight from frozen in the sealed bag, dropped into hot water — the eel steams gently and the glaze does not scorch, which is exactly what happens if you put frozen kabayaki under a grill. Frozen food stays safe indefinitely at −18 °C; the months are about quality, and the oily flesh is what limits them.
en.thawing: Reheat from frozen in the sealed bag in hot water, or thaw in the fridge overnight. Never thaw it on the counter, and do not refreeze a portion you have already reheated.
spoilage: A sour or fermented smell over the sweet soy one.
A slimy or tacky surface under the glaze.
A rancid, paint-like smell — the eel fat has oxidised.
A puffed or leaking vacuum pack, or any mould.
tips: Freeze the pack unopened; it reheats best that way.
Reheat in hot water in the bag rather than under a grill.
Decant an opened pack into a covered box and note the date.
Keep it away from milk and butter; the glaze carries the smell.

faq.q: How long does kabayaki keep once opened?
faq.a: 3–4 days at 4 °C (40 °F) or below in a covered box. Unopened, follow the pack's printed date.
Yes, 1–2 months at −18 °C, ideally in the unopened pack. Reheat from frozen in the bag in hot water.

faq.q: Does the sweet glaze preserve the eel?
faq.a: No. It is sugar and soy on the surface of a moist cooked fish. Kabayaki is a chilled or frozen food throughout.

faq.q: What is the best way to reheat kabayaki?
faq.a: In its sealed bag in hot water, straight from frozen or chilled. A grill scorches the glaze before the eel is hot through.

zh.name: 蒲燒鰻
zh.summary: 蒲燒鰻是鰻魚剖開、蒸過、燒烤後刷上甜醬油醬汁的產品，以真空包冷藏或冷凍販售。包裝完好時依標示日期；開封後冷藏 3～4 天，冷凍 1～2 個月。
zh.pantry: 蒲燒鰻是冷藏或冷凍的熟食，不是常溫品。那層甜醬看起來像保存手段，其實不是：它只是抹在一條含水、全熟、又很油的魚表面的糖和醬油。從冷藏櫃買的真空包，就繼續放冷藏。拿出來後守 2 小時原則，廚房超過 32 °C 時為 1 小時；請確實加熱再吃，不要一邊等飯熟、一邊讓它溫溫地放在檯面上。
zh.fridge: 未開封請依包裝自己的標示日期，那個日期反映的是包裝與製程，比我們能給的任何數字都長。真空包一拆開，它就只是熟魚：加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下，3～4 天內吃完，這是「熟魚」的公告值。請遠離氣味重的食物，醬汁很會吸味。要吃請確實加熱透，同一份也不要反覆加熱又放涼。
zh.freezer: 蒲燒鰻在 −18 °C 下可放 1～2 個月。盡量整包未開封冷凍，或把分好的份量連醬汁一起包緊。最好的復熱方式是連密封袋一起直接從冷凍丟進熱水裡——鰻魚會被溫和地蒸熱，醬汁也不會燒焦，而那正是冷凍蒲燒鰻直接進烤箱會發生的事。−18 °C 下安全性是無限期的，月數講的是品質，決定它的是那些油脂。
zh.thawing: 連密封袋直接從冷凍泡熱水復熱，或放冷藏隔夜解凍。不要放室溫解凍，已經加熱過的那份也不要再次冷凍。
spoilage: 在甜醬香之外出現酸味或發酵味。
醬汁底下的表面變得黏滑。
出現油耗、油漆般的氣味——鰻魚脂肪已經氧化。
真空包鼓脹或滲漏，或出現任何霉。
tips: 整包未開封冷凍；那樣復熱效果最好。
連袋泡熱水復熱，不要直接進烤箱。
拆開的包裝倒進有蓋容器並記下日期。
遠離牛奶和奶油；醬汁的氣味會轉移。

faq.q: 蒲燒鰻開封後可以放多久？
faq.a: 加蓋容器放 4 °C 以下 3～4 天。未開封請依包裝標示日期。
可以，−18 °C 下 1～2 個月，最好整包未開封冷凍。復熱時連袋直接泡熱水。
不行。那只是塗在含水熟魚表面的糖和醬油。蒲燒鰻從頭到尾都是冷藏或冷凍食品。
連密封袋泡熱水，不論是冷凍還是冷藏都適用。用烤箱的話，醬汁往往在魚熱透之前就焦了。
